t.6.73.1: Then, in that situation, Rāvaṇa's younger brother spoke to Lakṣmaṇa words that were harmful to the enemies and that would accomplish their purpose.
t.6.73.2: Strive, Lakṣmaṇa, to break apart this great army; once it is broken, the son of the lord of the Rākṣasas will also become visible here.
t.6.73.3: So you, showering the enemies with arrows like Indra's thunderbolt, rush at them swiftly, before this rite of mine is brought to completion.
t.6.73.4: O hero, slay Rāvaṇi, that wicked-souled and unrighteous one, devoted to sorcery, cruel in his deeds, who brings terror to all the worlds.
t.6.73.5: Hearing the words of Vibhīṣaṇa, Lakṣmaṇa, marked with auspicious signs, rained down showers of arrows upon the son of the lord of the rākṣasas.
t.6.73.6: The bears and the monkeys, fighting with trees and the finest of mountain rocks, rushed together against that army standing arrayed before them.
t.6.73.7: And the Rākṣasas, eager to slaughter the army of the monkeys, came on together with sharpened arrows, swords, spears and lances raised aloft.
t.6.73.8: That tumultuous clash arose between the monkeys and the Rākṣasas, making Laṅkā resound on every side with its mighty uproar.
t.6.73.9: The sky was covered with weapons of many kinds and shapes, with sharpened arrows and trees, and with dreadful mountain peaks held aloft.
t.6.73.10: Those rākṣasas, with distorted faces and arms, plunging their weapons into the vānaras, caused them very great fear.
t.6.73.11: In the same way, the monkeys, with whole trees and with mountain peaks, attacked and struck down the foremost of the rākṣasas in battle.
t.6.73.12: As the rākṣasas were being slain by the foremost of the bears and monkeys, huge of body and mighty in strength, a great fear arose among them.
t.6.73.13: Hearing that his own army was dejected and harassed by the enemies, the invincible one rose up, since that task still remained unaccomplished.
t.6.73.14: Emerging from the darkness of the trees, that rākṣasa Rāvaṇi, his anger aroused, mounted his chariot, which stood ready and had been yoked beforehand.
t.6.73.15: He, bearing a fearsome bow and arrows, resembling a heap of black collyrium, with red mouth and eyes, cruel, shone forth like Death, the Ender.
t.6.73.17: At that time Hanumān, the subduer of foes, who resembled a mountain, lifted up a huge tree that was most difficult to withstand.
t.6.73.18: Burning up that army of the rākṣasas like the fire of universal destruction, that vānara in battle rendered it senseless with many trees.
t.6.73.16: But as soon as it saw him standing in his chariot, that army of rākṣasas of terrible impetuosity, eager to fight with Lakṣmaṇa, turned around.
t.6.73.19: As soon as they saw Hanūmān, the son of the Wind, wreaking destruction with great force, thousands of rākṣasas showered him with missiles.
t.6.73.20: Those bearing sharp spears struck with spears, those with swords in hand with swords, those holding javelins with javelins, and those armed with paṭṭisas with paṭṭisas.
t.6.73.21: With iron-studded clubs and maces, with lances bright to behold, with śataghnīs by the hundreds, and with iron hammers too.
t.6.73.23: Having approached him from all sides, they struck him, who was like a mountain; and he too, greatly enraged, wrought a great slaughter among them.
t.6.73.22: With terrible axes and with javelins, with fists as swift as the thunderbolt and with slaps of the palm like lightning-strikes, the rākṣasas struck.
t.6.73.24: Indrajit saw the son of the Wind, the best of monkeys, like a mountain, the slayer of foes, slaughtering his enemies.
t.6.73.25: He said this to his charioteer: "Drive to where this monkey is, for if he is left unchecked he will surely bring about the destruction of us rākṣasas."
t.6.73.26: Thus addressed by him, the charioteer drove to where Māruti stood, bearing Indrajit, the supremely invincible, who was stationed in the chariot.
t.6.73.27: Approaching, that invincible rākṣasa rained down arrows, swords, spears, blades and battle-axes upon the head of the monkey.
t.6.73.28: Having received those terrible weapons, Māruti, possessed by great fury, spoke these words.
t.6.73.29: Fight, if you are a hero, O evil-minded son of Rāvaṇa! Having come up against the son of Vāyu, you will not return alive.
t.6.73.31: Vibhīṣaṇa pointed out to Lakṣmaṇa the son of Rāvaṇa, who, with his bow raised, was seeking to kill Hanūmān.
t.6.73.30: Fight with your two arms, if you would have single combat with me in battle! Withstand my onslaught, O fool, and then you will be the foremost of the rākṣasas.
t.6.73.32: He who is the conqueror of Vāsava, the son born of Rāvaṇa himself, that very one, having mounted his chariot, seeks to slay Hanūmān.
t.6.73.33: O Saumitri, slay that son of Rāvaṇa with your terrible arrows of matchless form, which tear foes apart and bring an end to life.
t.6.73.34: Thus addressed by Vibhīṣaṇa, the terrifier of foes, the great-souled one then beheld him standing in his chariot, huge as a mountain, of fearsome strength and hard to assail.
